title: Hosted agents overview
summary: A hosted agent is your own agent code, packaged as a container image or a .zip, that Foundry runs with a dedicated endpoint, a dedicated Entra identity, scaling and session state.
useIf: You bring code, a framework, custom protocols, persistent files or need to choose compute size.
avoidIf: Instructions, a model and tools already cover the behavior, or the code must stay on another cloud.

explain.md: Hosted agents are containerized agentic apps that run on Agent Service. Your code does the orchestration and calls models from the Foundry catalog for reasoning [[r2]]. Supported languages are Python and C#, and the docs name Agent Framework, LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Anthropic Agent SDK and the GitHub Copilot SDK, or custom code [[r1]]. You ship a container image, or a .zip of source that Foundry builds into an image [[r1]].

On deploy the service pulls the image from Azure Container Registry, assigns a **dedicated Entra agent identity** and exposes a **dedicated endpoint**. At runtime it provisions compute **per session** in a VM-isolated sandbox. Your code can call Foundry models, Toolbox tools and downstream Azure services with the agent identity [[r2]]. The split is clear: you own the code inside the sandbox, the platform owns the endpoint, identity, scaling and session state around it [[r2]].

explain.title: Who owns what
explain.alt: A client calls a dedicated endpoint. Agent Service holds versions, identity and conversations and starts a per-session sandbox with your code. The code calls models, a toolbox and Azure services.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  C[Client] --> E[Dedicated endpoint]
  E --> AS[Agent Service: versions, identity, state]
  AS --> SB[Per-session sandbox: your code]
  SB --> M[Foundry models]
  SB --> TB[Toolbox]
  SB --> AZ[Your Azure services]

explain.caption: Why choose hosted over a prompt agent (from the hosted agents page)
head: Need
How hosted agents answer it
rows: Any framework or custom code instead of prompt-only definitions
Webhooks and non-OpenAI payloads through the Invocations protocol
Choose CPU and memory for the session sandbox
`$HOME` and the `/files` endpoint persist across turns
Preview resilience features keep in-progress work across process interruptions

explain.title: Status and migration, checked 2026-10-13
explain.md: The Foundry GA table has no separate hosted agent row and the concept page has no preview banner, so an explicit "hosted agents are GA" statement is **UNVERIFIED** [[r9]]. Long-running resilience articles are preview [[tr2]]. Support for the initial-preview hosted backend ended on 2026-08-20. Redeploy needs `azure-ai-projects` 2.3.0 or later and `azd` 1.23.0 or later with `azd ext install azure.ai.agents`, and the adapter packages were replaced by `azure-ai-agentserver-responses` and `azure-ai-agentserver-invocations` [[r11]]. The docs list 31 regions on this date and say the list grows [[r2]].

whereToUse: An existing LangGraph, Agent Framework or OpenAI Agents SDK app that needs a managed endpoint, identity and scaling
Agents that receive webhooks, run batch extraction or expose AG-UI streaming
Agents that need `$HOME` files across turns, such as a working directory or cached data
Agents that call your own code or private services using the agent identity with explicit RBAC

use: You need code, a framework or a custom protocol
You need to choose CPU and memory per session
You want Foundry to own identity, scaling and observability around your code
avoid: The agent is light and a prompt agent would do, since hosted adds compute billed per active session
The code must stay on another cloud or on premises
Your policy needs a documented GA label for every component and the hosted status is unconfirmed
flips: Sustained high concurrency of heavy agents flips the cost dial: concurrency times allocation drives the bill
A requirement to run in another cloud flips you to self-hosting with registration for governance
Only a webhook or batch need appears: still hosted, but use Invocations rather than Responses

pitfalls.symptom: A guide tells you to set a capability host or use a shared endpoint with `agent_reference`
pitfalls.cause: It targets the initial-preview backend that ended on 2026-08-20
pitfalls.fix: Follow the migration page: dedicated endpoint per agent, new adapter packages, redeploy [[r11]].

pitfalls.symptom: Agent cannot reach your storage account after deploy
pitfalls.cause: The agent identity only gets model inference and session storage by default
pitfalls.fix: Assign RBAC roles to the agent identity for any other resource [[r2]].

pitfalls.cause: Oversized sandbox multiplied by concurrent active sessions
pitfalls.fix: Right-size per version. The docs advise a larger size only if sustained peaks pass about 70 percent of allocation [[r2]].

scenarios.title: Graph agent needs a managed home
scenarios.situation: A team has a working graph-based agent in Python. They want an endpoint, an Entra identity and scaling without running a cluster.
unknowns: How many concurrent active sessions at peak?
scenarios.question: Where do you run it?

options.name: Hosted agent
options.why: Keeps your framework and code and adds a dedicated endpoint, agent identity, scaling and session state.
options.tradeoff: Compute is billed per active session and the hosted GA label is unconfirmed.

options.name: Self-host on Container Apps
options.why: Full control and it works anywhere.
options.tradeoff: You wire identity, scaling, session persistence and observability yourself.

options.name: Rebuild as a prompt agent
options.why: The graph logic does not fit configuration and would be lost.
options.tradeoff: Right when the logic is a simple tool-calling loop.

flips.if: The agent is a plain tool-calling loop
flips.then: Prompt agent, and drop the container.

flips.if: Policy forbids anything without a GA label
flips.then: Self-host until the hosted status is confirmed for you.

scenarios.takeaway: Hosted fits existing code that wants a managed endpoint and identity.

scenarios.title: Spiky Q&A at high concurrency
scenarios.situation: A stateless question-and-answer agent sees thousands of short sessions at peak and almost none overnight.
scenarios.question: Which runtime do you choose?

options.name: Prompt agent
options.why: No compute line: you pay for inference and tools, and Foundry scales it.

options.name: Direct Responses API call from an existing app
options.why: Also avoids sandbox compute and keeps the definition in code.
options.tradeoff: You host and secure the caller.

options.name: Hosted agent at the largest sandbox
options.why: Billing follows CPU and memory across active sessions, so oversizing multiplies cost by concurrency.
options.tradeoff: Right when sessions need code, files or heavy local compute.

flips.if: Each session needs a working directory or custom code
flips.then: Hosted agent, sized at the smallest tier that holds the peak.

flips.if: Concurrency is low and logic is complex
flips.then: Hosted cost is small, so code flexibility wins.

scenarios.takeaway: Hosted cost is concurrency times allocation, so match the runtime to the work.

quiz.q: Which needs are listed by the docs as reasons to choose a hosted agent over a prompt agent?
options: Bring your own code or framework
Use custom protocols such as webhooks
Persist files and state across turns with `$HOME` and `/files`
quiz.explain: The hosted agents page lists own code, custom protocols, compute control, stateful files and resilient long-lived work. Hosted adds compute, so it does not avoid billing.

quiz.q: An initial-preview hosted agent stopped working after 2026-08-20. What is the correct fix?
options: Redeploy on the new model with a dedicated endpoint and the new adapter packages
Raise the idle timeout to 60 minutes
Add a second identity to the project
quiz.explain: Support for the initial-preview backend ended and redeploy is required. Idle timeout, identities and protocol choice do not address a retired backend.

quiz.q: Which change most directly flips the choice from a hosted agent to a prompt agent?
options: The behavior now fits instructions, a model and tools
quiz.explain: A prompt agent covers behavior expressed as configuration. The other three are the reasons hosted agents exist.

flashcards.front: What does Foundry create automatically when a hosted agent is deployed?
flashcards.back: A dedicated Microsoft Entra agent identity and a dedicated endpoint. Publishing is not needed for programmatic access.

flashcards.front: Is there an explicit GA statement for hosted agents (checked 2026-10-13)?
flashcards.back: UNVERIFIED. The GA table has no hosted row and the concept page has no preview banner. Confirm status before a GA-only policy decision.

flashcards.front: How are hosted agents billed beyond inference?
flashcards.back: CPU and memory consumed across active sessions. Numeric rates are on the pricing page and are UNVERIFIED in this guide.
